# Costco Wholesale (COST): Long Equity Thesis — Membership Compounding and International Expansion as Underappreciated Earnings Engines

---

## Executive Summary

- **Variant view**: Consensus models Costco's membership fee income as a largely static recurring stream punctuated by discrete price increases. The structural reality is a three-layer compounding engine — member count growth, Executive tier mix-shift, and periodic fee repricing — that collectively compounds fee income at 10–12% annually with near-100% incremental gross margin. This compounding is independent of merchandise sales growth and is underrepresented in consensus EPS forecasts of 8.9% CAGR.
- **International margin premium is not priced**: The "Other International" segment (China, Japan, UK, Korea, Australia, Spain, France) operates at a **4.01% operating margin vs. the US's 3.37%** — a 64-basis-point structural premium — yet consensus assumes international expansion is margin-dilutive. International segment operating income is growing at **12.1% YoY vs. US at 9.4%**, and the segment's share of total operating income (33%) already exceeds its share of revenue (27.6%).
- **Business quality is exceptional**: ROIC of 15.9% (FY2025) against a WACC of ~8.5% yields a sustained 6–7 percentage point value-creation spread. ROE has ranged 27–31% over FY2019–FY2025. Kirkland Signature reached **\$90 billion in sales in FY2025** (~33% of total revenue), growing approximately 1 percentage point of penetration per year.
- **Valuation is full but defensible at \$900–\$950**: At ~\$1,000–\$1,040 (June 17, 2026), the stock trades at 45x forward FY2026 P/E and 30.8x EV/EBITDA — 57% above the 10-year average P/E of ~32.5x. The upside case (Argus \$1,200, Goldman Sachs \$1,171) requires sustained 11–13% EPS compounding and successful international execution. The bear case (Simply Wall St DCF \$784, Alpha Spread \$581, Basis Report \$897) hinges on multiple compression rather than business deterioration.
- **Primary catalyst not in models**: The next membership fee increase — estimated 2029–2030 based on a 5–5.5 year historical cadence — represents an 8–10% overnight EPS step-function not embedded in current consensus, with post-hike 2-year stock returns of +32% (2017), +43% (2011), and +33% (2006).

## 1. One-Paragraph Thesis — Expected Upside and Time Horizon

Costco's durable competitive position rests on a membership flywheel that consensus systematically mismeasures. With **82.9 million paid members** (Q3 FY2026), a **92.2% U.S./Canada renewal rate** (implying ~13-year average tenure), and **41.2 million Executive members** growing at 9.6% YoY, the membership fee income stream — which management itself estimates at 60–70% of total operating profit — compounds at rates materially above consensus's implied linear extrapolation [[34]](https://www.mojosalesandbranding.com/post/costco-executive-membership-2026-roadshow-brand-strategy) [[25]](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/costco-cost-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/). In FY2026 Q1, the fee income line grew **14% YoY**, with only approximately half attributable to the September 2024 price increase; the remainder was organic, driven by new member acquisition and Executive tier upgrades [[2]](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/costcos-membership-income-growth-reinforces-155900727.html) [[5]](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/costcos-membership-model-continues-deliver-145900455.html). The international segment adds a second structural alpha source: 292 warehouses outside North America (31% of the base) produce a **64-basis-point operating margin premium vs. the US**, and management has committed to a 50/50 US-to-international split in annual warehouse openings at 30+ per year for the next decade [[8]](https://www.thestreet.com/retail/inside-costcos-plan-to-open-more-warehouse-stores) [[97]](https://stockdividendscreener.com/discount-stores/costco/costco-profit-margin-breakdown/). A 3–5 year holding period should capture: (1) continued membership fee compounding at 10–12% annually as Executive penetration advances from 48.8% toward saturation, (2) margin leverage as international warehouses mature and renewal rates converge toward the 92%+ US level from the current 89.7% worldwide rate, (3) the next fee increase (estimated 2029–2030) as an unmodeled EPS catalyst, and (4) Kirkland Signature's continued penetration from 28% toward 35% of net sales. The bull case price targets (\$1,200–\$1,315 from Argus and Goldman Sachs respectively) imply **15–26% upside** from current levels on a 2–3 year horizon; on a 5-year view with compounding EPS growth of 11–13%, the returns could be materially higher if multiple compression is limited [[58]](https://ts2.tech/en/costco-cost-stock-december-1-2025-news-analyst-targets-and-2026-outlook/) [[60]](https://ts2.tech/en/costco-stock-cost-news-forecasts-and-analyst-outlook-for-2026-whats-driving-shares-on-dec-24-2025/).

## 2. Business Quality — Economic Moat, Unit Economics, Returns on Capital, Reinvestment Runway

### 2.1 Economic Moat: Structure and Durability

The U.S. warehouse club channel is a near-perfect oligopoly: three operators control a **\$308.7 billion market** (2025), with Costco holding **63.7% share (\$197B revenue)**, Sam's Club 29.2% (\$90.2B), and BJ's Wholesale 7.0% (\$21.5B) [[18]](https://www.mmcginvest.com/post/costco-vs-sam-s-club-in-2026-a-comparative-analysis-of-the-u-s-warehouse-club-market). The structural barriers to entry are formidable — the membership fee itself is a switching cost mechanism. With a 92.2% U.S./Canada renewal rate, the implied average member tenure of approximately 13.2 years (calculated as 1 ÷ (1 − 0.077)) creates a near-permanent revenue annuity [[35]](https://www.i4a.com/blog/calculating-member-lifetime-value/).

Costco's moat is reinforced by three interlocking mechanisms:

1. **The membership fee model**: Annual dues create a selection effect — members who pay \$65–\$130 annually are pre-committed to shopping at Costco, elevating basket sizes (\$96 average spend per visit vs. Sam's Club's \$79) and visit frequency (32 trips/year vs. Sam's Club's 20) [[18]](https://www.mmcginvest.com/post/costco-vs-sam-s-club-in-2026-a-comparative-analysis-of-the-u-s-warehouse-club-market). Members who feel they are not recouping the fee self-select out, keeping the renewal base highly engaged.

2. **SKU discipline**: Approximately **4,000 SKUs vs. Walmart's 140,000+** enables Costco to command outsized supplier leverage, negotiate bulk pricing that cannot be replicated at smaller volumes, and curate a "treasure hunt" merchandise experience that drives incremental purchase behavior.

3. **Kirkland Signature**: At **\$90 billion in FY2025 sales** (approximately 28% of net sales per PLMA data, gaining ~1 percentage point annually), Kirkland is simultaneously a margin lever and a switching cost. Members cannot replicate Kirkland product quality and pricing elsewhere — particularly given Costco's policy of pricing Kirkland items **20% below comparable national brand alternatives** while maintaining equal or superior quality [[20]](https://www.mojosalesandbranding.com/post/kirkland-signature-expansion-2026-brand-strategy). CEO-level sign-off is required for every new Kirkland SKU, institutionalizing quality control [[96]](https://www.tastingtable.com/2042169/how-much-kirkland-products-make-sales-per-year/).

## 3. What Consensus Is Missing — The Non-Obvious Insight

### 3.1 Membership Fee Compounding Is a Layered Flywheel, Not a Step Function

The Street models membership fee income as: (base members × flat fee) + occasional price increase. The structural reality is a three-layer compounding mechanism:

- **Layer 1 — Member count growth**: Paid memberships have grown from 56.5M (FY2019) to 82.9M (Q3 FY2026) — a 4–6% annual growth rate [[6]](https://capitaloneshopping.com/research/costco-statistics/) [[25]](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/costco-cost-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/).
- **Layer 2 — Executive tier mix-shift**: Executive members (at \$130/year vs. Gold Star \$65/year) are growing at 9.6% YoY — materially faster than the total member base. Penetration has moved from 45.4% (FY2023) to 48.8% (Q3 FY2026). Each percentage point of Executive penetration gains \$65 of incremental annual fee revenue per converted member. With 82.9M total paid members and penetration at 48.8%, a 5 percentage point shift (to 53.8%) adds approximately \$810M in incremental annualized fee revenue with near-100% gross margin.
- **Layer 3 — Discrete fee increases**: Every 5–7 years, the company raises dues 8–10%, flowing immediately to the P&L. The critical insight from Q1 FY2026: only approximately half of the 14% membership fee growth was attributable to the September 2024 price increase; the other ~7% was organic [[2]](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/costcos-membership-income-growth-reinforces-155900727.html) [[55]](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/costcos-membership-fees-rise-14-sustainable-growth-or-peak). This means the base is growing at 7% without any fee increase — the price increase is additive to an already-compounding baseline.

Consensus treats Layer 3 as the sole driver and Layers 1 and 2 as background noise. This systematically understates the earnings power.

As international warehouses mature (particularly Japan at 37 locations, Canada at 115, Korea at 20, Australia at 15), the segment mix shift compounds consolidated margins. This dynamic is absent from most analyst models.

### 3.3 China's Executive Membership Launch Is the Maturation Unlock — Not Modeled

China's membership renewal rates at the Shenzhen Longhua warehouse were reported at 60–70% as of July 2025 — a 22–32 percentage point gap vs. the US 92% [[72]](https://www.eyeshenzhen.com/content/2025-07/23/content_31638596.htm) [[73]](https://www.szlhq.gov.cn/english/DigitalLonghua/News/content/post_12302025.html). Consensus reads this as a structural failure. The variant interpretation is different: US and Canadian warehouses exhibited similar early-stage renewal challenges before the Executive tier deepened member engagement. Costco launched **Executive Membership in China during Q3 FY2026** — the precise mechanism that, in the US, drove Executive member penetration to 74.3% of sales [[32]](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/COST/pressreleases/2202621/costco-q3-earnings-beat-on-strong-membership-and-digital-growth/). If China mirrors the US trajectory over 5–7 years, the renewal uplift from Executive tier adoption could eliminate the gap entirely, transforming the China operation from a drag to a structural margin contributor. With 7 warehouses and management characterizing China as "the most consequential emerging market," the optionality is enormous and entirely unmodeled by consensus.

### 3.4 Next Fee Increase Is an Unmodeled EPS Catalyst

The September 2024 fee increase was the first in seven years. Historical cadence: September 2000, May 2006, November 2011, June 2017, September 2024 — approximately every 5.5 years on average. The next increase, on this cadence, arrives in approximately 2029–2030 [[90]](https://www.fool.com/investing/2024/07/20/history-says-costco-will-do-this-after-fee-hike/). Consensus EPS forecasts extend through FY2027 without incorporating this catalyst. Historical post-hike 2-year stock performance: +32% (2017 increase), +43% (2011 increase), +33% (2006 increase) [[90]](https://www.fool.com/investing/2024/07/20/history-says-costco-will-do-this-after-fee-hike/). The asymmetry is that the market typically ignores this until the announcement, then rereates the stock materially higher.

### 3.5 Retail Media and AI-Powered Conversion Are High-Margin New Revenue Lines

In Q3 FY2026, management disclosed that personalized AI-driven product recommendation carousels contributed to **"just under \$5 billion of e-commerce sales"** and achieved **3x the conversion rate** of typical traffic [[25]](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/costco-cost-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/). The first off-site retail media campaign launched Q1 FY2025, with **approximately 10 partners live by Q2 FY2025** and "many more in the pipeline" [[21]](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2025/03/06/costco-wholesale-cost-q2-2025-earnings-call-transc/). This high-margin (near-100% incremental margin on recommendation-driven sales) revenue source is not separately modeled in any consensus estimate reviewed. Traffic from AI-driven search is growing by triple digits, albeit from a small base [[30]](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/INTC-Q/pressreleases/2318869/where-will-costco-stock-be-in-3-years/).

## 4. Growth Drivers — Volume, Pricing, Share Gain, New Markets, Margin

### 4.1 Volume and Traffic

Q3 FY2026 reported **shopping frequency +2.4% worldwide** and **average transaction up 7.3%** (+4.2% excluding gas and FX) [[25]](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/costco-cost-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/). E-commerce comparable sales grew **+21.5% (Q3 FY2026, digitally-enabled)** with site and app traffic up 37% YoY. Full-year FY2025 e-commerce comparable sales were +15.6% [[83]](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/costco-wholesale-corporation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-operating). Half of new members are under 40 years old, providing decades of renewal duration ahead [[23]](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/costco-sales-topped-250-billion-fiscal-2024-less-2-those-sales-are-key-understanding).

### 4.2 Pricing Architecture

The pricing lever operates on two tracks: merchandise pricing (philosophical restraint, "first to lower, last to raise") and membership fees (periodic step-function). Q3 FY2026 illustrative price reductions: Kirkland Crispy Wings \$16.99→\$14.99, Kirkland Milk Chocolate Almonds \$19.99→\$18.99, Kirkland golf balls \$32.99→\$29.99, Kirkland king-size sheets \$89.99→\$79.99 [[25]](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/costco-cost-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/). This restraint on merchandise pricing directly protects renewal rates and member value perception, which is the mechanism through which membership fee increases go uncontested — the September 2024 hike produced essentially no churn (U.S./Canada renewal rates went from 92.7% pre-hike to 92.2% post-hike, a 50-basis-point decline that management attributes to a higher share of digitally-acquired younger members, not price sensitivity) [[54]](https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2025/oct/17/costco-tested-members-with-higher-fees-the-results/) [[1]](https://www.detroitnews.com/story/business/retail/2025/10/18/costco-tested-members-with-higher-fees-the-results-are-in/86769123007/).

### 4.3 Share Gain Dynamics

The NBER academic working paper on warehouse club pricing effects provides a revealing competitive distinction: Costco entry raises incumbent grocery prices by **1.4–2.7%** (suggesting Costco attracts high-income, non-price-sensitive members who then patronize premium incumbents), while **Sam's Club entry has no statistically significant effect** on competitor pricing [[19]](https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w17220/w17220.pdf). This implies Costco's member base is structurally more loyal and affluent — median household income \$110–125K vs. Sam's Club \$75–80K — creating a virtuous reinforcement loop where higher member spending (\$3,086/year at Costco vs. \$1,583 at Sam's Club) strengthens Costco's negotiating power with vendors, which improves product value, which reinforces loyalty [[18]](https://www.mmcginvest.com/post/costco-vs-sam-s-club-in-2026-a-comparative-analysis-of-the-u-s-warehouse-club-market).

### 4.5 Margin Trajectory

Operating margin has expanded from 2.11% (FY2021, distorted by \$283M incremental COVID safety costs) to 3.85% (FY2025) — a 174-basis-point improvement in 4 years [[84]](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/cost/financials/) [[83]](https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/costco-wholesale-corporation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-operating). ## 9. Bear Case — What Could Go Wrong and Exit Conditions

### 9.1 The Primary Risk: Valuation, Not Business Quality

The bears' most compelling argument is not operational — it is valuation. At **49.5–52x trailing P/E** (57% above the 10-year average of ~32.5x), Costco is priced as a perpetual compounder. Under the Basis Report base case, assuming 7% revenue growth and slight margin expansion, the model generates only a **5.6% IRR** after a 4.4% annual P/E compression [[62]](https://simplywall.st/community/narratives/us/consumer-retailing/nasdaq-cost/costco-wholesale/jnurtlec-update-for-costco-wholesale). The bear case (Basis Report: \$897, 0.6% IRR) requires merely margin compression from 3.1% to 2.9% operating margin with 6.6% annual P/E compression — no business failure required. Simply Wall St's fair P/E of 37.82x vs. current 51.82x implies a 27% overvaluation; Alpha Spread's DCF yields \$581.12 (40% overvalued) [[63]](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/consumer-retailing/nasdaq-cost/costco-wholesale/news/has-costco-cost-become-too-expensive-after-its-strong-year-t) [[64]](https://www.alphaspread.com/security/nasdaq/cost/summary).

### 9.2 Seven Bear Case Risk Pillars

**1. U.S. Warehouse Saturation**

With 629 U.S. warehouses at FY2025 year-end (California alone hosts ~143, or 23% of the US base), incremental US openings increasingly serve excess demand from existing 300M+ annual-sales locations rather than truly greenfield markets [[66]](https://www.mmcginvest.com/post/costco-wholesale-s-u-s-operations-in-2025-footprint-and-performance) [[27]](https://www.foxbusiness.com/retail/costco-plans-major-growth-push-targeting-30-new-locations-annually). The 15 net new US warehouses annually imply 2.4% unit growth on a maturing base — insufficient to drive material revenue acceleration without comp sales momentum.

**2. China Renewal Rate Structural Gap**

The Shenzhen Longhua warehouse renewal rate of **60–70%** (warehouse manager statement, July 2025) represents a **22–32 percentage point gap vs. the US 92%** [[72]](https://www.eyeshenzhen.com/content/2025-07/23/content_31638596.htm) [[73]](https://www.szlhq.gov.cn/english/DigitalLonghua/News/content/post_12302025.html). If this reflects structural product-market fit challenges (smaller Chinese household sizes, mobile HK-Shenzhen member population, competition from Alibaba's Hema Fresh with 30-minute doorstep delivery), scaling from 7 to 50+ China warehouses would drag global renewal metrics meaningfully. At 50 China warehouses with 60% renewal vs. 90%+ everywhere else, the consolidated worldwide renewal rate faces approximately 100 basis points of structural headwind — directly compressing fee income growth.

**3. Sam's Club Competitive Erosion**

A March 2024 price comparison across 60 items (Raleigh, NC) found **Sam's Club at \$777.42 vs. Costco at \$833.08** — a 7.2% price gap in Sam's Club's favor [[65]](https://www.newsobserver.com/news/business/article286872310.html). An AARP study found Sam's Club **15% cheaper** on bulk groceries [[17]](https://www.foodrepublic.com/1939265/cheapest-wholesale-grocery-chain/). Sam's Club raised its membership fees in May 2026 — just 3.5 years after its prior increase vs. Costco's 7-year gap — suggesting Sam's Club is actively monetizing its member base more aggressively. If Costco's affluent member base becomes more price-sensitive in a recessionary environment, the Sam's Club proposition closes rapidly.

**4. Labor Cost Inflation Locked In**

The March 2025 three-year employee agreement locked in: minimum wage \$20/hr, top-of-scale assistants \$30.20/hr, top-of-scale cashiers \$31.90/hr, with **\$1/hr raises in March 2026 and March 2027** [[76]](https://www.cfodive.com/news/costco-raises-minimum-hourly-wage-20-compensation/742075/) [[78]](https://fortune.com/2025/03/11/costco-workers-make-31-an-hour-raises-for-next-two-years/). CFO Millerchip explicitly characterized this as a "mid-single digit" SG&A headwind, with offsetting productivity improvements required to maintain margin trajectories [[76]](https://www.cfodive.com/news/costco-raises-minimum-hourly-wage-20-compensation/742075/). Combined with the capex step-up to \$6.0–6.5B (FY2026), operating margin expansion may be more modest than the 174-basis-point trajectory of FY2021–FY2025 suggests.

**5. Tariff and Supply Chain Exposure**

Approximately **one-third of warehouse sales derive from imported items** [[81]](https://www.mojosalesandbranding.com/post/costco-tariffs-2026-brand-strategy-roadshow-vendors-1). Key Kirkland Signature exposures include olive oil (20% EU tariff), Thai jasmine rice (37%), organic seaweed (25%), mixed nuts (10–46% depending on origin), and coffee (10–46%) [[79]](https://www.eatthis.com/costco-groceries-facing-new-tariffs/). While Costco has pivoted **70% of Kirkland Signature production to domestic manufacturers** [[80]](https://www.ainvest.com/news/costco-fortress-strategy-supply-chain-mastery-price-discipline-shielding-investors-tariffs-inflation-2506/) and the February 2026 Supreme Court ruling in *Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump* invalidated IEEPA-based tariffs (with Costco's potential tariff refund estimated at "hundreds of millions of dollars") [[81]](https://www.mojosalesandbranding.com/post/costco-tariffs-2026-brand-strategy-roadshow-vendors-1), implementation remains uncertain and staple categories like coffee have no viable domestic substitute.

**6. E-Commerce Dependency on Instacart**

Costco's digital strategy relies substantially on Instacart's infrastructure (Storefront Pro platform for same-day delivery; North American member credit program). Consumer Reports' December 2025 investigation revealed that **Instacart conducted AI-enabled price experiments at Costco**, with identical products priced differently across customers by \$0.07–\$2.56 in what Instacart internally called "smart rounding" — experiments Instacart stopped at Costco after the investigation [[75]](https://www.consumerreports.org/money/questionable-business-practices/instacart-ai-pricing-experiment-inflating-grocery-bills-a1142182490/). This third-party dependency creates brand trust risk that Costco cannot fully control. Amazon's August 2025 expansion of same-day perishable delivery to **1,000 cities and towns** escalates competitive pressure [[74]](https://www.grocerydive.com/news/amazon-instacart-same-day-grocery-delivery-ecommerce/757762/).

**7. Membership Growth Deceleration**

Paid member growth has decelerated: 5.2% (Q1 FY2026) → 4.8% (Q2 FY2026) → 4.1% (Q3 FY2026) [[5]](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/costcos-membership-model-continues-deliver-145900455.html) [[4]](https://www.thestreet.com/retail/costco-members-may-be-overlooking-this-valuable-feature) [[25]](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/costco-cost-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/). Management has acknowledged a "downtick in renewal rates" driven by younger, digitally-acquired members with "modestly higher churn rates" [[1]](https://www.detroitnews.com/story/business/retail/2025/10/18/costco-tested-members-with-higher-fees-the-results-are-in/86769123007/). If this trend reflects structural saturation in addressable markets rather than a temporary cohort effect, the 8.9% consensus EPS CAGR — which implicitly requires sustained 5–6% member growth — becomes difficult to achieve.

## 10. Position Sizing and Risk Framework

### 10.1 Risk-Adjusted Return Assessment

**Probability-weighted expected value analysis** (approximate, based on available analyst targets and DCF scenarios):

| Bull case (sustained 11–13% EPS compounding, membership flywheel accelerates) | 25% | \$1,250 | \$312.50 |
| Base case (consensus 8.9% EPS, modest multiple compression) | 50% | \$1,100 | \$550.00 |
| Bear case (growth deceleration, multiple compression) | 20% | \$897 | \$179.40 |
| Deep bear (execution failure, traffic plateau) | 5% | \$726 | \$36.30 |
| **Probability-weighted expected value** | **100%** | — | **\$1,078.20** |

At a spot price of approximately \$1,040, the probability-weighted expected value of approximately \$1,078 implies a **+3.7% upside** — approximately fairly valued, with the bull case providing meaningful optionality if the thesis plays.

**The thesis improves materially at entry prices of \$900–\$950** (where the bear case IRR becomes less punishing and the bull case IRR exceeds 20%). Tactically, accumulation on pullbacks to 40–42x forward P/E (approximately \$870–920 on current year EPS) is the preferred approach.

### 10.2 Position Sizing Framework

| Parameter | Recommendation | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Core position size (long-only)** | 3–5% of portfolio | World-class business; limited downside risk from business deterioration; primary risk is valuation |
| **Add trigger** | Pullback to 40–42x forward P/E (~\$870–920) | Risk-reward improves materially at lower multiples |
| **Trim trigger** | Rally to 57–60x forward P/E (prior all-time highs) | Valuation premium becomes untenable without EPS acceleration |
| **Hard sell trigger** | Any two exit conditions met simultaneously | Business model integrity breached |

### 10.3 Monitoring Dashboard (Ongoing, Not Episodic)

The variant thesis has specific metrics that either confirm or refute it on a quarterly basis:

**Monthly (with Costco's monthly sales releases)**:
- Total comparable sales: Must maintain >5% to support valuation
- International comparable sales premium vs. US: Currently +710 bps (Q2 FY2026); must stay positive

**Quarterly (with earnings)**:
- Membership fee income growth rate: Must sustain 10%+ to confirm compounding thesis
- Executive member penetration: Must continue advancing (target: 55% by 2028)
- U.S./Canada renewal rate: 92%+ threshold
- China renewal rate trajectory: Post-Executive Membership launch improvement
- SG&A % of sales: Must stay below 9.5% ceiling
- International segment operating margin: Must hold above 3.8% to validate structural premium thesis
- Operating cash flow conversion to FCF: Must sustain 55%+ OCF-to-FCF ratio

**Event-Driven**:
- China Executive Membership renewal rate (first full-cycle data expected FY2026 Q4 earnings, September 2026)
- Special dividend announcement (overdue; positive catalyst when announced)
- Any management commentary on next fee increase timing (significant positive re-rating event)
- Sam's Club competitive pricing changes or membership restructuring

### 10.4 Final Assessment

Costco is a world-class compounder trading at a full, though defensible, valuation. The variant thesis — that membership fee compounding and international expansion margin premiums are structurally underappreciated — has quantifiable support in the company's own disclosed financials: a 3-year average international operating margin premium of 64–135 basis points vs. the US, Executive member growth outpacing total member growth by 5 percentage points YoY, and a fee income line growing 10.7% in the most recent quarter even with the price increase contribution declining. The business would be compelling at a 20–25% lower entry price. At current levels, it warrants a core position with a horizon of 3–5 years, targeting the compounding of the membership flywheel and the optionality of the next fee increase — neither of which consensus has adequately modeled.

> **The central insight**: Consensus evaluates Costco as a retailer that happens to collect membership fees. The correct framework is a membership-fee business that operates retail as a distribution mechanism to perpetuate the membership. Under the first framework, 50x P/E looks stretched. Under the second framework, the question becomes whether a business growing its core annuity stream at 10–12% with 92% retention and international margin premiums deserves a premium to a compounder at 45x — and the answer depends almost entirely on whether the international expansion and Executive penetration theses continue to deliver.
